transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-10 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Sarah Li (Orchard), Rajiv Menon (Orchard), Emily Carter (Orchard PM), Tom Becker (Orchard Security)

Summary (auto): AE/SE led scoping to define quality evaluation plan for POC: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring approach, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to use this session to lock down the quality eval plan for the POC, so we can make sure we're measuring the right things and align on timeline and infra.
[00:12] Dr. Sarah: yep thanks, we have a hard requirement to reduce clinician editing time by at least 30% and keep hallucination rate below, uh, basically very low, can't be more than 1% for critical facts.
[00:24] Carlos: got it, so two main success criteria then — editing reduction and hallucination ceiling — we'll translate that into measurable metrics. quick Q: are you expecting structured outputs (like FHIR) or free-text summaries?
[00:38] Emily: both; core use case is templated discharge summaries where certain fields must match exact values (meds, dosages, allergies) and then a free-text summary where clinicians can edit.
[00:50] Rajiv: and from infra side we need to know expected QPS so we can size Dedicated or decide Hosted is fine. current peak is around 8 QPS for generation during shift change, average is ~1.5 QPS.
[01:05] Maya: cool that's helpful. for the quality eval plan we typically do: golden prompts (50-100 representative prompts), regression suite of synthetic edge cases, hallucination checks that compare model outputs to ground truth, format validators for FHIR fields, and a scoring rubric that's a weighted mix of exact match, semantic similarity, and hallucination penalty.
[01:21] Dr. Sarah: can you unpack the scoring? how do you weigh exact match vs semantic similarity? for meds we need exact; for summaries semantic similarity is fine.
[01:33] Lena: recommended approach: per-field rules — critical fields (meds, dosages, allergies) use exact match with binary pass/fail; templated sections use regex/format checks; narrative summary scored with BLEU or BERTScore plus human review sample. typical weights we propose: 40% critical-field exact match, 30% hallucination penalty (lower is better), 20% semantic similarity on narrative, 10% clinician satisfaction from a small blind review panel. but that is flexible.
[02:00] Tom: also want an audit trail — each inference should show model version, prompt, and token usage; we need KMS integration for keys and audit logs retained for 180 days.
[02:12] Carlos: yep Redwood supports KMS integrations and per-request metadata in logs; for Private/VPC we can also do customer-managed keys. small note — sometimes our transcripts say "Redwood Dedicared" — ignore, that was a slip, we mean Redwood Dedicated.
[02:28] Rajiv: on hallucination measurement, do you have an automated check?
[02:32] Maya: we do a mixture. automated entity-level checks: extract entities (meds/doses/dates) from output and compare to ground truth. any mismatch counts as a hallucination flag. then we run a secondary fuzzy-check for paraphrase differences. we also flag contradictions (e.g., says patient is allergic then lists med they are allergic to).
[02:48] Dr. Sarah: sounds good. what about golden prompts — how do you select them?
[02:52] Lena: we ask customers to provide 50-100 representative prompts and examples with expected outputs; we augment with synthetic edge cases (ambiguous notes, poor handwriting OCR input, trailing context). golden set covers high-frequency happy-path and top-known edge cases.
[03:08] Emily: we can get 200 anonymized prompts but will mark 75 as gold annotated by clinicians. timeline to deliver by Friday?
[03:15] Emily: sorry, by next Friday — 2026-04-17.
[03:18] Maya: perfect. for the POC timeline we propose a 6-week plan:
[03:22] Maya: Week 0: kickoff and infra (VPC + access), Week 1: ingest sample prompts and labelling, Week 2: initial model runs + baseline benchmarks, Week 3: tune batching/quantization and test Dedicated sizing, Week 4: run full golden set + regressions, Week 5: human review + business metric calculation, Week 6: final review and decision.
[03:45] Rajiv: that sounds reasonable. on sizing — with 8 QPS peak do you recommend Dedicated?
[03:50] Carlos: depends on latency SLO and cost target. if you need 95th p99 latency under 500ms for short prompts and consistent throughput, Dedicated is the safer bet. Hosted can work for lower SLOs and bursty workloads. we can run benchmarks both ways in week 2.
[04:06] Dr. Sarah: our SLO is: 95th latency under 1.2s for full discharge generation and typical cost target is less than $0.15 per generation.
[04:14] Lena: we will instrument per-route token cost and report both latency distribution and cost per 1k generations; Carlos will prepare a benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.internal/poc/orchard/benchmarks.xlsx) — note: placeholder link.
[04:29] Tom: security gating — SOC2 report and encryption at rest are required before production; for the POC we can accept a limited security review but will need full docs before any Dedicated deployment.
[04:40] Maya: we'll send SOC2 and the standard security packet; Tom, please flag any extra questions in that doc.
[04:46] Tom: will do.
[04:48] Dr. Sarah: about regression tests — we want a suite that runs on every model checkpoint to detect quality regressions. how do you surface regressions?
[04:56] Carlos: we run the golden set and compute the scoring rubric; if aggregate score drops more than a threshold (e.g., 3 points absolute or 5% relative) we mark as regression and alert the team. we also break down per-field failure rates so you can see which part regressed.
[05:12] Emily: want to include hallucination-specific thresholds for critical fields — e.g., zero tolerance for fabricated allergies or med substitutions.
[05:20] Maya: agreed. we'll add per-field gating rules: critical fields must be 99% exact match across the golden set.
[05:27] Rajiv: for format checks we need FHIR-lite validation — is that something Redwood provides?
[05:32] Lena: we have regex-based validators and can run a FHIR schema validator in the pipeline; we'll include a small adapter to map outputs to the expected schema.
[05:40] Dr. Sarah: scoring approach — will there be a dashboard?
[05:43] Carlos: yes Redwood Console will show per-prompt results, aggregated metrics, token costs, and a diff view for failed cases. we'll share a dashboard template.
[05:52] Maya: ok quick walk-through of acceptance criteria as we propose them: 1) Critical-field exact match >= 99% on golden set, 2) Hallucination rate <= 1% for critical facts, 3) Clinician editing time reduction >= 30% measured in a small live test, 4) Latency 95th under 1.2s, 5) Cost per generation <= $0.15.
[06:17] Emily: can we weight those into a single pass/fail score?
[06:20] Lena: yes we produce a score 0-100 with weights: critical-field 40, hallucination penalty 30 (lower hallucination increases score), semantic similarity 20, clinician satisfaction 10. pass threshold we usually set at 75.
[06:36] Dr. Sarah: sounds reasonable, but we may want critical-field weight higher; clinicians won't accept anything that risks meds.
[06:43] Maya: we can shift it to 50/25/15/10 if you want; we'll capture that as an open item for Emily and Sarah to confirm.
[06:52] Emily: we'll confirm by 2026-04-16.
[06:55] Rajiv: on data handling — we will only share de-identified prompts for POC; is that okay?
[07:01] Maya: yes, de-identified data is fine for quality eval; for production we'll discuss private deployment and ingestion controls.
[07:07] Tom: any notes on retention? For POC logs we need to ensure retention is limited to 30 days unless otherwise agreed.
[07:14] Carlos: we can configure log retention per-customer in Redwood Console. we'll set it to 30 days for the POC by default.
[07:20] Dr. Sarah: what about regression frequency? nightly? on every model checkpoint?
[07:24] Lena: by default we run the golden set nightly during the POC and on every new model checkpoint if you upload or we push a new model. results posted to the dashboard and a weekly summary sent to stakeholders.
[07:36] Maya: final practicals: Carlos will send benchmark spreadsheet and initial config, Maya will send SOW and pricing, Emily will send golden prompt annotations, Rajiv will set up VPC access for the Dedicated test cluster if we go that route.
[07:50] Dr. Sarah: any concerns about hallucination checks missing subtle errors?
[07:53] Carlos: automated checks won't catch everything; that's why we recommend a small human blind review sample (50-100 cases) each week to catch subtle errors and calibrate automated detectors.
[08:04] Emily: ok we can do that.
[08:06] Tom: security will review SOC2 docs and list extra items; hope to have those to you by 4/15.
[08:12] Maya: great, thanks everyone. do we want to capture next steps out loud?
[08:16] Emily: yes — SOW by 4/14, prompts by 4/17, confirm weights by 4/16, infra kickoff week of 4/20, Carlos benchmark by 4/20.
[08:27] Maya: perfect, we'll follow up in email with links and the SOW. thanks all.

End of transcript.
